entries.title: A property declared in a tool's notice that its code did not have
entries.published: The door probe's notice said it measured two channels separately, pull requests and issues, and reported both.
entries.truth: The code only read pull requests; the "issue" comments it counted were PR comments, and the JSON output had no issue field. A published 9/9 issue score had been counted by hand. Fixed the same evening: a pure issue classifier with four states never merged into the PR score, bench 33 to 48 cases.

entries.title: Repository "door" verdicts rendered on truncated lists
entries.published: Several external repositories were rated GREEN / RED / MUTE by the door probe, run without an API token.
entries.truth: Unauthenticated, the API truncates pull-request lists: on one repository the authenticated probe read 13 PRs where the anonymous one read 3. The numbers were right, the denominator was not. The probe now refuses to conclude without a token, and every cited door was re-measured with one.

entries.title: The house counted among the visitors
entries.published: A repository was given as a dead door because one of its pull requests had been open for 451 days.
entries.truth: Its three open PRs were from two collaborators and a bot: no outside contributor was waiting. The manual count mixed maintainers with visitors; the instrument partitions on who merged and rates the door ORANGE, which is not "closed to outsiders". The world had not moved, our measurement was wrong.

entries.title: An inference published in the present tense of an observation
entries.published: A public issue comment stated, in the present tense of an observation, that in a real browser the Cloudflare interstitial renders and then the site does, so the site is up.
entries.truth: We never saw the site. The browser rendered the interstitial and nothing else: zero later requests, zero real-content markers. Found by four refuters run against our own sentences, then corrected by editing the same comment 45 minutes later with a note saying what changed. The recommendation survived: treat a challenge header as inconclusive precisely because we do not know.

entries.title: A correct mechanism used as a wrong argument, in public
entries.published: A PR comment presented a configuration-time case as "the same shape" as the defect the PR fixed.
entries.truth: The cited state is set at execution time, not declared in policy, so no load-time check can reason about it; the parallel did not hold. Found two greps after posting by searching for what would break our own sentence, never by a run. Corrected by editing the same comment 25 minutes later, with a note.

entries.title: A graved "not posted yet" that had been posted for four days
entries.published: The journal said a reply on an OWASP thread was ready and not posted, and two later entries repeated it.
entries.truth: It had been posted four days earlier and was the last message of the thread, measurable by one API call. A graved line is true at its date and becomes a cache of unknown freshness the moment the world moves. A leftover that names a public surface is re-measured before being carried forward, never copied.

entries.title: A correct figure with its meaning inverted
entries.published: A paper's "-8.6 points" was read as the utility cost of adding a human approval gate.
entries.truth: In the paper, the interactive condition is the one WITH human approval, and -8.6 is better than the strict condition's -13.9: the gate gains 5.3 points, it does not cost 8.6. Caught by fetching the paper body before citing it; no public text ever carried the wrong reading.

entries.title: What an anonymous fetch can do is not what an account can do
entries.published: A draft said issue creation was restricted on a repository, on the strength of an unauthenticated fetch.
entries.truth: The form was open, and our issue #1 was created there the same evening. An anonymous fetch measures what an anonymous visitor can do, never what the account can do; the positive control was missing. Caught by the maintainer with a screenshot before the draft left.

entries.title: A remedy that existed and protected nothing
entries.published: The journal said a monitoring report no longer printed amounts it could not qualify, and that the fix was live in production.
entries.truth: The rendered object reduced the on-chain verdict to a boolean, so the "measurable" flag was always true and the report would have printed amounts even on a mute scan. The bench checked that the right strings existed in the source, not the flow of the value. Caught because the maintainer demanded a manual run instead of waiting for the cron; fixed and deployed the same day, with a flow check in the bench.

entries.title: A function selector written by hand in the sentence that forbade it
entries.published: A contract selector was quoted as one 4-byte value in prose, documentation and a bench.
entries.truth: Measured on three disjoint channels, the selector is a different value; the code always computed it at run time, so no behaviour was ever wrong, only prose. The bench could not catch it: it fabricated bytecode containing its own constant and then found it there. Structural remedy: the selector is computed in the bench, and a parity test refuses any 4-byte literal in the shared block.

entries.title: An off-by-one in a procedure, followed to the letter, targets an existing token
entries.published: A pre-flight step said the next token id equals the current total supply.
entries.truth: The contract increments first, so the next id is total supply plus one; measured on a live cycle (26 before mint, token 27 minted). Closed by an instrument that computes the id from the contract; the dated document keeps its wrong line and carries an erratum pointer instead of being rewritten.

entries.title: A tool alias assumed universal was directory-scoped
entries.published: Procedures used a named RPC alias everywhere.
entries.truth: The alias only exists inside one project directory; elsewhere the tool reads it as a file path and fails. Cost one failed mint attempt. The pre-flight instrument now emits the literal URL.

entries.title: A "sourced" 60 s ceiling pointing at a line that said nothing of the kind
entries.published: A tool-call ceiling was attributed to a specific source line, under a "sourced reason" label.
entries.truth: That line is an unrelated configuration guard. The ceiling was unsourced until it was measured: 60,000 ms to the millisecond. The architectural conclusion survived on its other, correctly sourced leg.

entries.title: A "fixed at construction" address that the owner could redirect
entries.published: The journal and the public site said the curator address was fixed in the constructor.
entries.truth: The deployed bytecode carries an owner-only setter for it. The address is initialised at construction and redirectable by the owner; the real debt is "not dynamic per auction". The false claim had crossed the journal and the public site before being caught by reading the bytecode.

entries.title: A self-audit that refuted a real 45-second window by looking at the wrong clock
entries.published: An earlier claim that the maintainer had only 45 seconds to confirm was declared false because the client had no timeout.
entries.truth: The server side had a 45,000 ms timeout and abandoned the pending action regardless of the client. The refutation aimed at the wrong clock; the self-audit that denounced "invented obstacles" was wrong on one of its two examples.

entries.title: True of the contract, false of the key ring
entries.published: Settlement was described as callable by any funded wallet, with no hardware device and no secret needed.
entries.truth: True of the contract; false in practice, because every funded wallet sat behind a hardware signer or a paper password and the free keys held zero ETH by design. No "free" path existed. Same family as E7: right property, wrong sentence.

entries.title: Not a false claim: a rule that was reversed
entries.published: A rule said canonical backups were purged after upload.
entries.truth: Reversed: the rule destroyed the version history of the document that carries the project's priority evidence, leaving the journal with weaker traceability than the code. Backups are now moved to a history folder and never purged.

entries.title: A capability the device has, and refuses to use for us
entries.published: The state of the art said the hardware device already knows how to sign a delegation.
entries.truth: On silicon, the device parses the delegation and refuses any target outside its allow-list: "Back to safety". True as a capability, false in practice for a bespoke contract; a whole path closed by a two-minute test on the device.

entries.title: A submission recorded as "frozen" that had been sent
entries.published: A status block listed a partner-program submission as unchanged and frozen.
entries.truth: It had been unfrozen and submitted two entries earlier, confirmed on screen by the maintainer. The error was introduced while assembling the status block, not while measuring.

entries.title: Eight months of solo work that were four
entries.published: Public texts spoke of eight months of continuous solo work.
entries.truth: The project started on 1 April 2026: about four months at the time. Corrected on the public project page; two locked applications still carry the error and cannot be edited.

entries.title: A green invariant suite covering an almost empty state
entries.published: A 54/54 invariant suite was presented as real coverage, tested under random sequences.
entries.truth: The campaigns produced one to three accepted bids, zero winning settlements and zero claims per run: six stateful invariants were green on a near-empty state, and the one that graved a regulatory decision had an empty loop body. Found by a sensitivity probe added the same day; the green was real, the coverage was not.

entries.title: A ceremony said to be wasted after the human confirm, that failed before it
entries.published: A handover said a stale-selector transaction would revert only after the human confirmation and password.
entries.truth: Gas estimation runs before the transaction is frozen and before any human is asked, so the failure surfaces first. But the guarantee is an ordering accident, not a guard: freezing gas or skipping estimation would move the failure back behind the confirm. The real vector for a burned ceremony is time, not the stale ABI.

entries.title: An "exhaustive" list of four components that were eight
entries.published: A handover listed the four remaining off-chain components as exhaustive.
entries.truth: Measured: seven code files and one document, including a validation bench that encoded the old interface, a verbatim copy of a scanner carrying the same defect twice, and three event decoders that appeared in no catalogue.

entries.title: A specification document three items out of date, left intact with a pointer
entries.published: A specification described an anti-sniping buffer, a sketched bid signature and a settlement name, and declared itself to be graved before the contract was written.
entries.truth: The buffer had been removed, the real signature and selectors differ, and the contract was already written. The document body is left byte for byte; an erratum sits at its head. A dated document receives a pointer, it is not rewritten.

entries.title: A contradiction and an arbitration that did not exist
entries.published: Two documents were said to contradict each other on cycle duration ("1 h vs at least 3 h"), presented as the only measured vector for a burned ceremony and as a decision for the maintainer.
entries.truth: One states a floor, the other satisfies it. The margin was also over-escalated: the worst anti-snipe case was presented as the common case. A prudence pointer, not a conflict erratum.

entries.title: A royalty figure wrong by one thousandth, and the cited source was what falsified it
entries.published: The facts register said 8.333 % creator royalty, under a source line claiming splits verified to the wei.
entries.truth: The on-chain value is 833 basis points, i.e. 8.33 %; the addition decides (8.33 + 45.835 + 45.835 = 100.000, where 8.333 gives 100.003). Found by reading a public note that faithfully copied the register: the copy was not at fault, the source was. Corrected at the source and publicly in the same pass.

entries.title: E16, one link further: the root is a frozen comment in the verified contract
entries.published: The E16 line stopped at the register and blamed it.
entries.truth: The root is the contract's own source comment ("833 for 8.333%"), which the register cited. The file is byte-identical to the source verified on chain, and a single whitespace change would break that verification. E16 is documented, not repaired: editing the comment would make the repository copy non-reproducible against the chain.

entries.title: Two successive causal explanations for a fault whose cause is unknown
entries.published: The journal explained a wrong rule first by a translation from a field still carrying an old hardening, then by a field that was never updated.
entries.truth: Both were false: the field carried the corrected version, measured before any rewrite. The cause of the original fault remains unknown; what got explained were the explanations. A causal explanation produced without measurement is a state assertion.

entries.title: "Ten months apart" was 39 days
entries.published: An article draft said two rule sets were elaborated ten months apart, and the journal graved it.
entries.truth: First commits: 20 June and 29 July 2026, 39 days. The whole project was four months old. Caught the same evening by the git audit of that very article; the article was corrected, the journal body stays intact and this line arbitrates.

entries.title: Three occurrences declared wrong, one of which was a target, and the real error was a sentence
entries.published: Three occurrences of a royalty figure on the public site were listed as wrong.
entries.truth: Two described the deployed contract and were wrong; the third described a future phase and was right, correcting it would have created a new falsehood. The uncounted error was a sentence that attributed the right number to the live contract. A count classifies numbers; a public surface is judged on its sentences.

entries.title: A suite said not to cover a requirement, after reading three files out of six
entries.published: A draft reply said a third party's conformance suite did not cover a requirement.
entries.truth: The suite's scenario file covers it. Absence declared outside the measured perimeter. Caught before sending; graved because a draft read as a source contaminates what follows.

entries.title: A paper version paired with the wrong date
entries.published: A reference cited version 2 of a preprint with the date of version 1.
entries.truth: Version 2 is dated two months later. Corrected before the archive deposit.

entries.title: A claim declared dead on all surfaces that lived on four more
entries.published: The journal declared a false public claim extinct on every surface after a grep and three article fetches.
entries.truth: It survived on the profile bio, the repository description, the profile README and the repository README, in other words than the grep looked for. Root cause: bio, description and profile repository were in no inventory at all. Produced the 23-surface inventory and its judge.

entries.title: A third extinction declared and refuted, this time by the surfaces judge on its first run
entries.published: The state block said the E16 figure was closed on all surfaces except its frozen root.
entries.truth: A public article still carried the wrong figure, 18 days later, two lines after describing the real settlement. Found by the surfaces judge on its very first pass, not by a reader. Corrected by the maintainer, adding the source the wrong version lacked.

entries.title: A hash-chained log does not prove that nothing is missing
entries.published: The registry specification said a chained log proves that no entry is missing, and the whole design rested on it.
entries.truth: Chaining proves the interior, not exhaustiveness: with nothing outside the file recording the expected head or count, full erasure, tail truncation and last-entry rewrite all re-verify green. Falsified by an adversarial review (confirmed 3/3) and corrected at the source before any public text carried it. What would close it is a witness the writer cannot rewrite.

entries.title: A human signature required, when the human gesture was an out-of-band confirmation
entries.published: The governance document, a public article and a paper draft said every commitment of funds requires a human signature made outside the system.
entries.truth: For the first two cycles the signature came from a keystore inside the server; the human gesture was a confirmation on a separate channel. An earlier fix had changed one noun and left the verb intact for three days on four surfaces. This is the origin of rule 12: a claim is checked in the code path, not in the wording.

entries.title: Nine prevented faults presented as proof, four of which had left an instrument
entries.published: A public article presented nine near-faults as evidence that prevention works, each with what stopped it.
entries.truth: Nothing false, and nothing verifiable: by the criterion of what measurement the prevention had caused, only four of nine had left an instrument a third party could re-run; two of the guards believed strongest lived in a scratch script rewritten every pass. The criterion came from an outside reader. The article stays; this line arbitrates any reuse of the nine.

entries.title: "Authentication required" given as the reason a surface could not be monitored
entries.published: The surfaces inventory said an article platform required authentication and had no public API.
entries.truth: A plain unauthenticated GET returns the full article body. The real cause was simpler: the public URL had never been captured. Nuance measured the same pass: readable is not monitorable, two identical requests return two different fingerprints.

entries.title: A contradiction built from a source that could not answer the question
entries.published: A few hours of prose said the vendor documentation contradicted a measurement about a model parameter.
entries.truth: The general API page does not list per-model restrictions; absence of mention was taken for absence of restriction. Measured the same evening from two hosts with a positive control: the parameter is refused for that model, the original measurement holds. The probe that decides is the one you must obtain, not the one you can write alone.

entries.title: A count obtained by subtraction instead of counting
entries.published: A draft said the discovery column was off by one entry on 18 of 25 errata.
entries.truth: The subtraction counted four undetermined lines as shifted; counted line by line the figure is 14 of 21. Caught by a second reader before publication, in the very pass that graved that attribution is not deduced.

entries.title: A bid attributed to a software keystore that was signed on the hardware signer
entries.published: A cycle table said the bid came from the server keystore.
entries.truth: The keystore bid key has nonce 0 and balance 0: it never issued a transaction. The bid came from the hardware-backed address. The wording was inherited from an earlier architecture and survived the change unread.

entries.title: No probe exists, because a reasoning has no version string
entries.published: A published methodological reserve said judge independence could not be measured, only declared.
entries.truth: The judgement has no version, the evidence it is drawn from does: record the observation instead of the conclusion and independence becomes computable at the point of use. Falsified by an outside reader replying to the reserve we had published; reading what others answer to our surfaces is the cheapest audit of our own gaps.

entries.title: A gesture graved before it was done
entries.published: The journal said a new judge had entered the instrument register and the dashboard.
entries.truth: Sealing the witness does not regenerate the register, and the dashboard entry had never been written: zero occurrences. A gesture graved in the future perfect while writing the fragment; no judge confronts a journal sentence with the state of the code it describes. Repaired before this line was written.

withheld.title: A section-reference token in the journal pointing at the wrong journal
Two hosts said to diverge with only one declared
A service reported stopped that was running
A configuration key reported absent that lived in a second block
A "0 hit" that was 1, in a permissions file that is not a configuration
Two canonical documents contradicting each other on who runs the deployment
